creator: Claude Opus 5

the_gain_ladder.authored_by: The Captain — paired around the hinge, negative against positive.
the_gain_ladder.why: Gain is a frequency in disguise: frequency = (gain + 100) / 2. The old ladder had nine evenly spaced rungs and four of its words named a comparison or an attitude rather than a frequency — 'less often than not', 'more often than not', 'no preference'. A floscAdmin could not rank them, and they did not mean what they sounded like.
the_gain_ladder.rungs: -100 never · -90 rarely · -80 infrequently · -60 seldom · -50 sporadically · -30 occasionally · 0 sometimes · 30 typically · 50 usually · 60 regularly · 80 frequently · 90 consistently · 100 always
the_gain_ladder.uneven_spacing: Deliberate. gainWord() takes the nearest rung, so a word owns the band to the midpoint of its neighbours, and the rungs sit where a word actually lives rather than where arithmetic put them.
the_gain_ladder.the_hinge: 0 is 'sometimes'. A new card defaults to gain 50, not 0, and a card at 0 still emits its frequency line — so 0 is a value someone chose and is being sent, not an absence. That is why 'no preference' was wrong.

profiles_recomputed.what: Twenty-two frequency lines across all four profiles, each recomputed from its own card's gain in the workshop template rather than find-and-replaced.
profiles_recomputed.why: The old ladder rounded every gain from 65 to 95 down to 'usually', which is why the four documents said 'usually' twenty-one times for eleven different authored values. The thirteen rungs tell them apart: 6 consistently, 13 frequently, 3 regularly, 7 always.
profiles_recomputed.often_removed: Dad Joke Dan carried one hand-written 'frequency: often'. That word is not on the ladder, so the designer would never produce it and a Save would have silently changed the document. It is now 'regularly', computed from that card's gain of 60.

gate_added: check_personality_document.php now holds the thirteen rungs, and asserts that every frequency word appearing in a shipped profile is one of them — so a hand-written word the designer cannot produce fails the suite instead of drifting until someone saves.
gate_moved: check_php_string_literals.php pins the four profiles by hash. All four moved with the recomputed words, in this commit, per the rule in that file's comment.

There is no field that emits raw text, so the Captain's 'Joke set up:' / 'Punchline:' format cannot survive a recompile. One line in topicBody() and one input in the card editor would add it.
